macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds interest rates steady
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest-rate target at 3.75%–4.00%. U.S. stocks rose modestly after the decision, while Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments were interpreted as suggesting no rapid series of rate increases is likely.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. stocks close higher after Fed decision
items.summary: The Dow gained 0.2% to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.3% to 26,549.85.[1][5]

items.title: Alphabet falls after earnings disappoint
items.summary: Alphabet shares dropped about 10%–11% in after-hours or premarket trading after quarterly advertising revenue fell short of expectations and the company reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion, intensifying concerns about the cost of its AI investments.[2][3]

items.title: Microsoft gains on strong Azure growth
items.summary: Microsoft shares rose in late trading after the company reported better-than-expected revenue, supported by growth in its Azure cloud-infrastructure business.[2][3]

items.title: U.S. inflation and labor data remain firm
items.summary: The personal-consumption expenditures price index rose 0.5% in September after increasing 0.3% in August, while initial jobless claims edged down to 194,000 for the week ended October 24.[1]

items.title: Global markets mixed after Fed and technology earnings
items.summary: European shares advanced in early trading, with Germany’s DAX up 0.8% and France’s CAC 40 up 1%, while Japan’s Nikkei rose 1.1%. U.S. futures were mixed as investors assessed Alphabet’s disappointing results and Microsoft’s stronger report.[5]

items.title: Samsung shares fall despite strong results
items.summary: Samsung Electronics declined 4.1% after reporting strong quarterly results, as investors reacted negatively to its latest shareholder-return arrangements; SK Hynix rose 2.6%.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies retreat amid heavy liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $81,000, while Ether and several large altcoins also declined. Reported crypto liquidations ranged from roughly $633 million to $951 million over the preceding 24 hours, depending on the data window.[1][3][6]

items.title: OCC publishes stablecoin rule effective January 2027
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency published rules governing permitted payment stablecoin issuers, foreign payment stablecoin issuers, and certain custody activities under its jurisdiction.[4][5]

items.title: Ripple receives approval for national trust bank
items.summary: Ripple reportedly received final OCC approval to establish a national trust bank that will manage reserves for its RLUSD stablecoin and provide institutional digital-asset custody services.[3]

items.title: South Korea blocks unregistered crypto-service websites
items.summary: South Korean authorities approved measures to block access to 27 websites operated by crypto-asset service providers that failed to meet registration requirements, including KuCoin and MEXC.[3]

items.title: Osmosis proposes burning 55.5 million OSMO
items.summary: An Osmosis governance proposal would burn 55.5 million OSMO from the community pool—about 7% of supply—subject to an October 30 vote.[2]

items.title: Curve Finance expands StableSwap to Stellar
items.summary: Curve Finance reportedly launched StableSwap on Stellar, marking its first deployment outside an Ethereum Virtual Machine-compatible network.[8]

items.title: Mirae Asset completes tokenized note issuance on Solana
items.summary: Mirae Asset Securities Hong Kong completed issuance of a six-month, U.S.-dollar-denominated floating-rate financing note on Solana for qualified institutional investors.[1]

items.title: Binance submits crypto-license application in Brazil
items.summary: Binance reportedly filed a crypto-license application in Brazil before a regulatory deadline, beginning a review process that does not guarantee approval.[7]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon for cybersecurity
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model focused on coding, cybersecurity, and multi-step problem-solving. Initial access is restricted to selected cybersecurity partners during a controlled rollout.

items.title: Mistral releases trillion-parameter open-weight model
items.summary: Mistral reportedly released weights for a trillion-parameter model called “Le Chonk,” positioning it for coding and cybersecurity use cases and emphasizing organizational control compared with closed models.

items.title: OpenAI announces discoveries in math, computer science, and physics
items.summary: OpenAI reported that its models produced new results in several scientific fields, including work it says challenges the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The claims could have implications for theoretical computer science and cryptography, though independent validation remains important.

items.title: NVIDIA releases open transcription model for 40 languages
items.summary: NVIDIA released a free speech-to-text model supporting up to 40 languages. The model is designed for recorded audio applications such as meetings and medical transcription rather than live transcription.

items.title: Google DeepMind previews Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Genie 4, a research-preview world model with audio, more realistic simulated environments, and real-time steering through text prompts. Access is initially limited to trusted testers.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly launched GPT-6.1 Terra for visual reasoning and computer-use tasks, with pricing positioned below earlier GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol models.

items.title: Anthropic adds enterprise AI spending transparency tools
items.summary: Anthropic introduced reporting tools that give enterprise customers more detail about AI usage costs and productivity, targeting organizations seeking to measure returns from adoption of Claude Code and other services.

items.title: Microsoft reports record revenue driven by cloud and AI
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly posted $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue, marking its tenth consecutive quarter of record revenue, with cloud demand and AI-related services identified as major contributors.

items.title: Upwind raises $400 million for AI-driven cloud security
items.summary: Cloud-security company Upwind raised $400 million in Series C funding at a reported $3.8 billion valuation, choosing to remain independent after declining a buyout offer from Datadog.

items.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings agrees to acquire ADT
items.summary: Thrive Holdings reportedly agreed to buy home-security company ADT for $15.3 billion, with plans to apply artificial intelligence to ADT’s services and operations.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: BioWare closed by EA; next Mass Effect discontinued
items.summary: Electronic Arts has reportedly shut down BioWare after 30 years and discontinued development on the next Mass Effect game.

items.title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game launches Patch 4 and esports partnership
items.summary: Patch 4 adds redesigned versions of Aang and Korra, new attacks, and permanently available stages. The game is also starting weekly online tournaments with a $5,000 prize pool.

items.title: Company of Heroes 3 announces Operation Torch campaign DLC
items.summary: Relic Entertainment announced a new narrative-driven campaign expansion, Operation Torch, scheduled for release on PC on November 25, 2026.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla to receive New Game+
items.summary: Ubisoft announced that Assassin’s Creed Valhalla will add New Game+ on November 5, nearly six years after its original release.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 reaches new Steam player peak
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 reportedly reached a Steam player peak not seen since the Phantom Liberty expansion, driven by renewed interest surrounding Edgerunners and Update 2.5.

items.title: Aloft and Conan Exiles Enhanced announced for PS5
items.summary: Funcom announced that both survival games are planned for PlayStation 5 in early 2027.

items.title: Holochess launches for XREAL AURA
items.summary: Resolution Games released the mixed-reality tactical game Holochess alongside the launch of XREAL AURA spatial glasses.

items.title: Star Trek: Voyager – Across the Unknown receives Delta Chronicles 2 DLC
items.summary: Daedalic Entertainment and gameXcite released the third DLC pack for Star Trek: Voyager – Across the Unknown, available separately and through the Expansion Pass.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple launches touchscreen MacBook Pro
items.summary: Apple introduced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, featuring a redesigned chassis and a tandem OLED display. The laptop starts at $2,899 and uses M5 Pro and M5 Max chips; AI-specific details are excluded.

items.title: Microsoft reports record quarterly revenue
items.summary: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, marking its tenth consecutive quarter of record revenue. The company also disclosed Azure revenue of $33.2 billion, though related AI developments are excluded.

items.title: Samsung launches W27 foldable phone in China
items.summary: Samsung launched the China-market W27 foldable smartphone, starting at 18,999 yuan. The device includes satellite-communication support and two storage configurations.

items.title: Samsung says 2027 high-bandwidth memory capacity is sold out
items.summary: Samsung told investors that its 2027 high-bandwidth memory capacity has been sold out and that broader DRAM supply could remain tight into 2028. AI-specific context has been omitted.

items.title: Meta faces major financing plans for data-center expansion
items.summary: Meta is reportedly planning up to $95 billion in stock offerings, including a $60 billion at-the-market program. The reported purpose is AI infrastructure, so the AI-specific aspect is excluded from this summary.
